samples.summary: Design doc still states the board toolbar has NOT adopted the focus-release hook, but this change adopts it
samples.evidence: docs/design/slides/slides-keyboard-shortcuts.md:162-165 — "Board carries its own copy of the same `<button>` branch (`packages/frontend/src/app/board/is-editable-target.ts`); the attribute is opt-in, so the board toolbar can adopt the hook when that surface is verified." The diff adds `useCanvasFocusRelease()` + `data-canvas-toolbar` to `packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-toolbar.tsx:137,186`, so this paragraph (and the surrounding "called by the desktop slides toolbar" wording at line 143) now describes the old contract. The docs-link CI check only verifies backticked paths resolve, not prose accuracy, so nothing else catches this.

samples.summary: Active task doc's "Out of scope" section explicitly excludes the board toolbar, which this change now includes
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260819-slides-toolbar-focus-release-todo.md:49-55 lists the board's `is-editable-target.ts:27` branch as out of scope and says "board can adopt the hook later without touching this change", while `packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-toolbar.tsx:137` adopts it in this very change. The task file's Tasks checklist also has no board item, so the plan of record and the code now disagree.

samples.summary: Board's documented "Space on a focused BoardToolbar toggle activates the button instead of entering pan mode" guarantee is defeated for pointer users by the new hook
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/board/is-editable-target.ts:6-13 documents the BUTTON branch as existing "so Space on a focused `BoardToolbar` toggle still activates the button instead of entering pan mode", and it is consumed at packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:625. With `useCanvasFocusRelease()` now installed on the board toolbar (board-toolbar.tsx:137), a pointer-clicked toggle (e.g. Select / Text box / Insert image, board-toolbar.tsx:257,273,356) is blurred to `document.body` one task later, so a following Space enters pan mode instead of re-activating the toggle. The behaviour may be intended, but the out-of-diff module's stated rationale and its unit test intent (packages/frontend/src/app/board/is-editable-target.test.ts:55) no longer match the shipped interaction.

samples.summary: `menu-focus.ts`'s documented contract that Esc/outside-click dismissal falls through to Radix's focus-to-trigger no longer holds inside canvas toolbars
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/menu-focus.ts:20-29 documents: "Should we force that restoration even when the user dismissed the palette by clicking outside or pressing Esc? No … Outside-click and Esc fall through to Radix's default focus-to-trigger." Every consumer of that helper that lives inside the newly-marked toolbars (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/shape-controls.tsx:60, border-picker.tsx:72, text-element-controls.tsx:62, table-controls.tsx:103, fill-picker/gradient-editor.tsx:307) is now inside `[data-canvas-toolbar]`, where the hook blurs the trigger after an Esc dismissal too (a pointer-opened menu keeps `pointerDriven === true` through Escape — the new test at packages/frontend/src/components/toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:100-106 asserts exactly that). The deliberate distinction the shared module documents is therefore no longer observable in slides/board; the comment should be updated or the hook should honour it.

samples.summary: Shared-document (share-link editing) mounts `SlidesToolbar`, so the new document-level focus stealing also ships to that surface unreviewed
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:436 and :566 render `SlidesToolbar` for share-link editors (two separate render sites in the same file). Both now install the document-wide pointerdown/keydown/focusin capture listeners and blur toolbar buttons to `document.body`. Nothing in the diff, the design doc, or the task file mentions this consumer; if both toolbars can ever be mounted simultaneously the hook's listeners and deferred blur run twice per interaction. Worth confirming the shared-editing surface behaves as intended (its canvas is the same SlidesEditor, so it probably does, but it is an unreviewed consumer).
